title: Live GPS updates are linkable to the same child over time
description: Regular transmission of precise GPS coordinates from the child's device to the backend enables the backend, and anyone with access to the data stream or stored records, to link multiple location reports to the same child and reconstruct persistent movement patterns.
assumptions: The backend can associate repeated updates with the same device, account, session, token, network identifier, or other stable identifier.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best estimate for linkability of multiple messages/records about the same data subject.

title: Identity of the child may be inferred from precise location traces
description: A sequence of live GPS coordinates can reveal home address, school, and routine stops, allowing the child to be identified directly or indirectly even if explicit names are not sent in the flow itself.
assumptions: The location precision and update frequency are sufficient to infer habitual places, and the backend or another party can correlate those places with external information.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for identifiability via quasi-identifiers/inference; exact node naming may vary.

title: Continuous GPS feed discloses sensitive whereabouts and behavior
description: Live coordinates disclose the child's real-time whereabouts, routes, routines, and potentially sensitive visits or activities, exceeding what may be necessary for some service purposes and exposing highly sensitive personal data.
assumptions: The backend stores, processes, or otherwise has access to the coordinates in identifiable or linkable form.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for information disclosure of location data; exact LINDDUN Pro node may differ.

title: Child may be unaware of the extent and frequency of live location collection
description: If the app does not clearly communicate that precise GPS coordinates are sent at regular intervals to the backend, the child or guardian may not understand the ongoing observation and resulting privacy impact.
assumptions: Notice may be incomplete, unclear, or not presented in a child-appropriate manner; guardian consent/awareness mechanisms may be insufficient.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for lack of awareness/transparency; exact node id may vary.

title: Regular collection of precise child geolocation may exceed consent or legal basis
description: Sending live GPS coordinates for a child at regular intervals may be unlawful or non-compliant if not strictly necessary, not covered by valid consent or another legal basis, or if retention, minimization, and children's privacy obligations are not met.
assumptions: The system processes children's precise geolocation, which is typically subject to heightened legal and policy requirements.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for absence of legal basis/consent or broader policy non-compliance; exact LINDDUN Pro node naming may differ.

title: Long-term linkability of location pings to the same user/device
description: Storing each location ping in a persistent history store enables records from the same backend account, device identifier, or pseudonymous token to be linked over time, allowing construction of a continuous movement profile.
assumptions: Location pings include a stable or re-linkable identifier, account reference, device token, or metadata that permits correlation across records.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best fit for linkability via persistent identifiers in stored records; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode naming may vary.

title: Identification of individuals from stored location history
description: Fine-grained location history can identify a person directly or indirectly by revealing home/work locations, habitual routes, or visits to unique places, even if explicit names are absent.
assumptions: Stored pings are sufficiently granular in space/time and can be associated with one individual or small household.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for direct/indirect identification from quasi-identifiers in data; exact subnode may differ.

title: Disclosure of sensitive habits, places, and inferences from location history
description: The location history store contains raw pings from which observers can infer sensitive information such as residence, workplace, religion, health status, political activity, social relationships, and routines.
assumptions: Location history is accessible to internal services, operators, analysts, or attackers beyond the minimum necessary scope.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for information disclosure from stored content and derived inferences; exact LINDDUN Pro node may differ.

description: The backend writes each location ping to persistent storage, creating a detailed historical trail that may exceed what is necessary for the stated purpose if sampling, aggregation, minimization, or expiration controls are absent.
assumptions: Not all raw pings are strictly necessary for the service purpose, or retention duration is longer than needed.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for data minimization/retention concerns due to over-collection and persistent storage; exact subnode naming may vary.

title: Collection and storage of location history may exceed user expectations or consent
description: Writing every location ping to a history store may be incompatible with the consent obtained or with contextual expectations if users were not clearly informed about continuous collection, storage, granularity, downstream use, or retention.
assumptions: User notice/consent and purpose limitation for continuous location-history storage are incomplete, ambiguous, or absent.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for non-compliance relating to consent, transparency, and purpose limitation; exact node id may differ.

title: Users may be unaware of the existence and extent of stored location history

If access is granted without strict necessity checks, least-privilege scoping, or context-based restrictions, more precise or more frequent location data than needed may be disclosed, exposing sensitive movement patterns of the child.
assumptions: Assumes the secondary guardian may not always need continuous precise live location and that granularity/retention/access scope could be limited.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best fit for unauthorized or excessive disclosure on a data flow; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may vary by catalog version.

title: Secondary guardian may be unaware of location-sharing scope and conditions
description: If the backend grants access without clearly communicating what location data is shared, at what precision, how often, and for how long, the secondary guardian may misunderstand the extent and limitations of the processing. This can lead to uninformed use and poor privacy expectations management.
assumptions: Assumes notice/transparency to the receiving guardian is in scope for this flow.
uncertainty_note: Unawareness is somewhat indirect for this data flow because the recipient is the guardian rather than the child; exact node mapping may differ.

title: Location sharing to secondary guardian without valid consent or authorization basis
description: Granting a secondary guardian access to a child's live location may violate privacy requirements if the backend does not verify an appropriate legal/policy basis, parental authorization, custody constraints, or the child's applicable rights before sharing. The disclosure could therefore be non-compliant with consent and access-governance obligations.
assumptions: Assumes policy or legal rules restrict which guardians may access live child location and under what conditions.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit non-compliance node; exact node id may differ depending on whether the LINDDUN Pro tree distinguishes consent, purpose limitation, or access legitimacy in separate subnodes.

title: Secondary guardian can repudiate receipt or use of child's live location
description: If the system does not maintain reliable logging or acknowledgment of when live location access was granted and used, the secondary guardian may later deny having received or viewed the child's location. This weakens accountability for sensitive access and may hinder dispute resolution.
assumptions: Assumes access events are not strongly logged or bound to the guardian identity.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit repudiation node; exact subnode may vary depending on whether the threat tree separates sending, receiving, and access-event repudiation.

title: Live location enables identification and inference of child's habits and whereabouts
description: Even if the recipient already knows the child, sharing live location from the backend can reveal highly sensitive information such as home, school, routines, religious attendance, medical visits, or social relationships. The flow therefore increases identifiability and inference risks for the child.
assumptions: Assumes location updates are sufficiently precise or repeated to reveal patterns.
uncertainty_note: Identification and inference often overlap for precise location data; chosen node is a best estimate.

title: Repeated live location updates allow linking of child's activities over time
description: Continuous or repeated location disclosures to the secondary guardian can be linked across time to build a detailed activity trail. This allows correlation of separate events into a single behavioral profile of the child.
assumptions: Assumes the flow provides multiple updates rather than a single one-time location disclosure.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit linkability node for correlating multiple location disclosures over time; exact subnode may differ.

title: Partner can link analytics reports to other datasets or campaigns
description: Even if the backend shares aggregated usage and engagement analytics, the advertising/analytics partner may combine cohort-level metrics, app identifiers, campaign metadata, timestamps, geography, or publisher identifiers with other data it already holds, enabling linkage of this app's analytics to other datasets and potentially to identifiable segments or users.
assumptions: Shared analytics include stable app/account/campaign identifiers, sufficiently granular time or segment dimensions, or repeated reports that can be correlated with the partner's existing data.
uncertainty_note: Node id is my best fit for linkability via data combination on a disclosure flow; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree label may differ.

title: Supposedly aggregated analytics may still allow inference about individuals or small groups
description: If aggregates are reported for small cohorts, rare events, narrow time windows, or fine-grained dimensions, the partner may infer behavior, interests, or presence of particular users from the shared analytics.
assumptions: Aggregation thresholds, k-anonymity, noise injection, or suppression are absent or weak; partner can observe repeated reports over time.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for identifiability/inference from aggregate disclosures; exact tree node may vary.

title: Sharing analytics with a third party discloses user behavior beyond user expectations
description: Usage and engagement metrics derived from user activity are disclosed from the backend to an external advertising/analytics partner. This expands access to behavioral data outside the service's direct operational boundary and may reveal sensitive app usage patterns or audience characteristics.
assumptions: Users may not reasonably expect third-party sharing for monetization, and the partner is a distinct controller or processor with its own analytics/advertising interests.
uncertainty_note: Chosen as a general disclosure-of-information-on-data-flow node; exact node id may differ in the specific LINDDUN Pro catalog.

title: Users may be unaware that backend analytics are shared for advertising-funded monetization
description: The existence, purpose, scope, and recipients of this analytics sharing may not be visible to users, especially if described only broadly in privacy notices. Users may therefore not understand that their activity contributes to reports sent to an advertising/analytics partner.
assumptions: Notice is incomplete, hard to find, or uses vague wording such as 'trusted partners' without explaining monetization and categories of data shared.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for unawareness/lack of transparency; exact LINDDUN Pro node numbering may differ.

title: Analytics sharing may lack a valid legal basis or exceed stated purposes
description: Using app usage data to fund a free tier via an advertising/analytics partner may be incompatible with the original collection context, may exceed consent obtained, or may not satisfy purpose limitation, data minimization, or third-party sharing obligations under applicable privacy law.
assumptions: The service relies on consent or legitimate interests without proper balancing, or the privacy notice/controls do not clearly cover this partner sharing.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for non-compliance/legal-basis and purpose-limitation concerns; exact subtree identifier may differ.

title: Repeated aggregate reports may enable differencing attacks
description: Even if each report is aggregated, repeated disclosures over time or across overlapping segments can allow the partner to subtract one report from another and learn information about a small group or even an individual event.
assumptions: Reports are shared periodically with overlapping dimensions, and no contribution bounding, thresholding, or differential privacy controls are applied.
uncertainty_note: This is a disclosure threat grounded in differencing against aggregates; node id is approximate.

title: Interception of child's SOS message and precise location in transit
description: The child sends a manual check-in or SOS message together with current location to the backend. If transport protection is weak or misconfigured, an attacker on the network path could learn highly sensitive content: the fact that the child triggered SOS, the message itself, and the child's real-time location.
assumptions: Assumes the flow traverses networks where interception is possible and that transport/session protection may be insufficient or bypassed.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id. I am confident this is an Information Disclosure threat, but the exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may vary by threat tree version.

title: Linkability of repeated check-ins and SOS events to the same child
description: The backend can correlate repeated manual check-ins and SOS submissions, linking multiple location-bearing events over time to the same child account or device. This enables reconstruction of movement patterns, routines, and behavioral profiles.
assumptions: Assumes the backend receives stable identifiers such as account id, device id, session id, or other correlators alongside the message.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact LINDDUN Pro numbering for linkability-by-identifier/correlation may differ.

title: Identifiability of the child from message metadata and location
description: Even if the payload were partially minimized, the combination of child account context, device/network metadata, timestamp, and precise location can make the child directly or indirectly identifiable to backend operators or anyone gaining access to the received data.
assumptions: Assumes the backend has access to account, device, IP, timestamp, or similar metadata in addition to location and message content.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact subnode for identifiability from quasi-identifiers may vary.

title: Detectability that a child is in distress or performing a safety check-in
description: The mere arrival pattern, endpoint use, message size, timing, or event type may reveal that the child initiated a manual check-in or SOS, even before reading full content. This leaks sensitive state about the child's situation or routine.
assumptions: Assumes observers at the backend or with access to logs/traffic metadata can distinguish this flow from ordinary traffic.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact detectability node may differ depending on whether the tree distinguishes content from traffic-analysis signals.

title: Disclosure of personal habits and whereabouts through stored SOS/check-in history
description: Once received, the backend may retain check-in/SOS messages and precise locations. Over time this history reveals habitual routes, home/school locations, schedules, emergencies, and other intimate patterns about the child.
assumptions: Assumes messages and location history are stored, logged, backed up, or analytically processed beyond immediate delivery.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact disclosure-of-information subnode for stored history/inference may vary.

title: Unawareness of secondary use or retention of SOS and location data
description: The child may not understand how long the backend keeps SOS/check-in content and location, who can access it, whether it is used for analytics, or whether it is shared onward. This creates a risk that the child is not meaningfully aware of the privacy impact of sending the message.
assumptions: Assumes transparency notices are absent, unclear, not child-comprehensible, or not presented at the moment of data capture.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact unawareness subnode depends on the threat-tree version and whether it distinguishes retention, sharing, and purpose opacity.

title: Processing of child precise location and distress data without valid consent or other lawful basis
description: This flow processes special-context child data: precise geolocation combined with a safety/distress signal. If the backend collects or uses this data without appropriate parental authorization, child-specific transparency, purpose limitation, minimization, retention limits, or another valid lawful basis, the processing may be non-compliant.
assumptions: Assumes applicable child-privacy or data-protection obligations apply to the service and that governance controls may be insufficient.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact non-compliance node structure differs across LINDDUN Pro variants and applicable legal regimes.

title: Child can later be unable to prove what SOS/check-in data was sent
description: If the flow lacks reliable evidence, timestamps, or integrity-protected receipts, the child may be unable to demonstrate what message and location were actually submitted, or whether it was altered or lost before reaching the backend. This undermines accountability in a safety-critical context.
assumptions: Assumes no end-to-end acknowledgement, tamper-evident logging, or user-visible submission record exists.
uncertainty_note: This is a plausible non-repudiation/accountability-related privacy threat, but I am less confident it is a core LINDDUN concern for this flow than the others, and the exact node id is uncertain.
